history.content: Is it possible to search for Cloud Directory users in the App ID dashboard using their email addresses?

Yes, it is possible to search for Cloud Directory users in the App ID dashboard using their email addresses. Here are the steps to do so:
1. Go to the Cloud Directory > Users tab of your App ID instance.
2. Look through the table or search by using an email address to find the user that you want to see the information for. The search term must be exact.
3. In the overflow menu in the user's row, click View user details. A page opens that contains the user's information.

Cloud Directory is a scalable registry provided by IBM Cloud App ID for managing users. It enhances security and offers self-service options for your app's users. These users are linked to Cloud Directory as an identity provider, allowing them to sign up for your app using various configured identity provider options, or they can be added directly to your directory.User information in Cloud Directory can be viewed as a JSON object through APIs or the dashboard.

Cloud Directory provides a range of features that enhance user experience and security for your app. With Cloud Directory, you can:
- Improve your app's security with email verification.
- Offer users greater control through customizable sign-up and sign-in widgets and flows.
- Customize your app's appearance with personalized user interfaces and workflows.
- Gain deeper insights into user behavior by integrating App ID with your email provider.
You can manage the level of self-service allowed in your application using the service dashboard. These settings can be updated at any time and will automatically reflect in your app without needing to change your code or redeploy your application. 
Additionally, you can toggle options before users are added to your directory.

Yes, there are more features available in Cloud Directory. You can replace the default App ID sign-in and sign-up UIs and flows with customized options to support your brand recognition and policies. You can also add extra fields to the sign-up flow, validate the password length by policy, and accept only specific email addresses or check emails against a blocklist. You are able to configure the forgot password process and enable single sign-on (SSO) to provide your users a smooth authentication experience between multiple web apps. App ID provides SSO for Cloud Directory users, so if enabled, your users do not need to reenter their credentials every time they sign-in.
How can I manage directory settings?

You can manage Cloud Directory settings through the Cloud Directory dashboard. Here are some tasks you can perform:
1. Configure the level of self-service you wish to allow in your application, such as enabling users to change their account details and password using App ID's prebuilt screens.
2. Customize the default App ID sign-in and sign-up user interfaces and flows to reflect your brand identity and policies.
3. Set up the password recovery process.
4. Enable single sign-on (SSO) to provide your users with a seamless authentication experience across multiple web applications.
5. Manage user accounts and roles.
These settings can be updated at any time without needing to change your code or redeploy your application.
Do I need any special tools?
I do not have that information.
Managing verification methods and MFA factors

You can update or reset your authentication methods if the email address or phone number that you use to authenticate changes or becomes inaccessible by going to the [Verification methods and authentication factors](https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/mysecurity) page. If you encounter an "Incorrect validation code" error when trying to log in with an authentication factor, it means that one or more of your authentication factors are inaccessible. You can fix this by going to the same Verification methods and authentication factors page, validating your identity with two different verification methods, and then resetting your MFA factors if necessary.
How do I determine how many policies exist in my account?
You can check the number of policies in an account by using the CLI to ensure that you don't exceed the limit for your account.

How do you prevent Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks? What restrictions do you have in place? 

Neither third-parties nor the internet can see your transit gateway traffic. As no critical information, such as IP router addresses, is open to anyone but you, DDoS attacks cannot bring down the network. In addition, a typical Multi-protocol Label Switching service (MPLS) uses packet filtering and applies access control lists (ACLs) to limit access. Only the ports with routing protocols from a specific area of the network can access the information.





 How does my transit gateway handle encryption for connectivity between VPCs? 

IBM Cloud Transit Gateway does not perform encryption; it only provides connectivity. Encryption between VPCs is your own responsibility.

It is an RFC-2547-based platform where the core network and network address are 100% concealed.

Can I extend the webhook time limit? 

No. The service that you call from the webhook must return a response in 8 seconds or less, or the call is canceled. You cannot increase this time limit. For more information about strategies for handling complex actions with a webhook, watch the video in [Making a programmatic call from dialog](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-dialog-webhooks).
